chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah from Abi Jamil from Isma'il ibn Abi Idris from Al-Husayn ibn Damrah from his father from his grandfather who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The legal rulings of the Muslims are based on three: a just testimony, or an decisive oath, or a prevailing Sunnah from the Imams of Guidance.'

key_terms.أئمَّةُ الهُدَى: Imams of Guidance (referring to the Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.يَمِينٍ قَاطِعَةٍ: Decisive oath (used as evidence in court)

ai.seo_question: What are the three sources of legal evidence in Shia Islam according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Attributed to Imam Ali (AS), this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* defines the triad of legal proof, elevating the Sunnah of the Imams to the status of decisive evidence alongside testimony and oaths. This establishes the theological basis for relying on Imami traditions as a primary source of Sharia, distinct from or complementary to the Quranic text. It underscores the Imam's role as the authoritative interpreter whose established practices carry binding judicial weight.
